identityTradability.exchangeName: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. - Common Stock

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI infrastructure demand
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Multi-gigawatt commitments from Meta and Anthropic plus Microsoft Azure deployment materially broaden the customer/deployment evidence for Instinct and Helios.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Full-stack platform breadth
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Helios integrates Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, Pensando networking and ROCm, with cloud, OEM and manufacturing partners supporting deployment.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Ecosystem and software adoption
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Anthropic's engineering collaboration explicitly targets ROCm optimization, while Microsoft and other partners provide additional workload/deployment paths.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Advanced packaging and supply execution
discovery-weak-signals.basis: AMD is investing heavily in Taiwan ecosystem and advanced packaging capacity, which both supports scale and highlights upstream execution dependencies.

expectations-execution.name: Execution versus narrative
expectations-execution.basis: Named multi-gigawatt customers, production Helios status and Azure deployment plans provide primary-source evidence beyond a purely aspirational roadmap.

expectations-execution.name: Expectation conversion risk
expectations-execution.basis: The largest commitments require future shipment, installation, software qualification and utilization before their economics are fully realized.

expectations-execution.name: Customer diversification
expectations-execution.basis: Meta, Anthropic, Microsoft, OpenAI and additional cloud/OEM partners create multiple independent routes for platform adoption.

expectations-execution.name: Capital allocation
expectations-execution.basis: AMD's up-to-$5B Anthropic investment and >$10B Taiwan ecosystem investment may deepen strategic alignment and capacity, but returns and timing remain future execution evidence.

riskEvidence.basis: Liquidity/cash generation offset valuation, dilution, commitments, supply dependencies, substitution and deployment-conversion risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC financial/governance filings, named issuer deployment evidence and current external valuation observation; future economics preserved as unknown.

scoreRecord.thesis: AMD is converting a broad CPU/GPU/network/software platform into exceptional Data Center growth and named multi-gigawatt AI deployments, supported by strong liquidity; the principal constraint is an extreme valuation plus supply, dilution and execution dependencies.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: At roughly $890B market value and ~139x trailing earnings, substantial future AI success is already embedded while customer warrants, external manufacturing dependencies and deployment conversion create downside asymmetry if execution slips.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and late-2026 Helios/MI450 deployment evidence showing whether announced capacity converts into realized revenue, margins and utilization.

items.risk: Issuer-origin releases dominate forward deployment evidence; announced multi-gigawatt plans are not treated as realized revenue.

Extreme valuation, customer-warrant dilution, large purchase/lease commitments, external foundry/packaging/HBM dependencies and competitive substitution can amplify downside if deployment conversion slips.
AMD controls important compute layers but remains structurally dependent on third-party manufacturing, packaging/memory and customer infrastructure buildout.
Large named deployment plans can overstate realized causal control if customer utilization or software economics fail to convert physical capacity into durable workload share.
Potential dilution from large strategic warrants is material and should not be hidden by deployment headlines.
Supply, packaging/HBM, power and infrastructure dependencies can delay revenue conversion even when end demand exists.
Customer concentration can rise as a small number of hyperscalers/frontier labs account for outsized AI deployment plans.
Competitive response from NVIDIA and custom accelerators can compress pricing, share and software leverage.
Announced gigawatt commitments are forward deployment plans; realized revenue depends on shipment timing, customer buildout, power, networking, packaging, memory and system integration.
AMD's competitive position still depends on software maturity and workload portability versus incumbent and custom-accelerator alternatives.
Large ecosystem investments and a committed strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic increase capital-allocation and counterparty/execution exposure.
Security-level valuation attractiveness is not asserted because no canonical live price or valuation input was available in the reviewed work item; this is non-gating.
Large forward deployment announcements can outrun realized economics if qualification, construction, power availability or customer utilization slips.
Competitive execution remains exposed to NVIDIA, custom silicon and other accelerator architectures, especially if software or system-level economics fail to meet customer expectations.

contradictions.claim: Exceptional realized growth versus extreme security valuation
contradictions.resolution: Both are preserved: operating evidence supports high momentum while current valuation receives a deliberately low opportunity component.

contradictions.claim: Strong full-stack breadth versus incomplete control of successor bottlenecks
contradictions.resolution: Both are true: AMD can capture more rack-level value while foundry, packaging/HBM, power and customer qualification remain outside full company control.

contradictions.claim: Large strategic commitments are simultaneously evidence of demand and sources of dilution/execution risk.
contradictions.resolution: Treat deployment agreements as positive demand evidence while separately carrying warrant dilution and realization risk; do not net them into a single narrative claim.

contradictions.claim: Strong named demand evidence versus incomplete economic realization
contradictions.resolution: Both remain true: primary sources establish substantial customer intent and production progress, while most large-scale deployments still require future conversion into installed and utilized capacity.
